Read a checkpoint directory back into results

read_checkpoints.Rd

Reconstructs the return value of measure() from disk without making any model calls. Use when a run completed but the return value was lost, or to inspect how far a killed run progressed.

Usage

read_checkpoints(dir)

Arguments

dir

A string giving the checkpoint directory.

Value

A fathom_results object, the two frames measure() returns and documents there. Rows arrive in whatever order the directory listing gives, so sort if order matters.

The attributes are read back off the stored payloads rather than stamped from the current session, so a corpus reports the run that produced it.

  • instrument is the instrument as it was when the run happened.

  • num_ctx is the ceiling that run used, not the one a run would get now. A resumed run keeps this, which is why mixing ceilings inside one corpus cannot happen silently.

  • exclusive says whether the instrument shared one distribution.

  • run_at says when the run happened, not when it was read.

A file that cannot be read is treated as absent rather than as an error, since a killed run can leave one half-written and re-extracting that document is the only recoverable reading. Errors when the directory holds no readable checkpoints at all.

Provenance

The context ceiling, the exclusivity flag and the run timestamp are read from disk rather than inferred from the current session. A run written under one ceiling reports that ceiling even if the current session would resolve a different one.

See also

measure(), whose checkpoint argument writes what this reads.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs a running Ollama server, so it is not run here.
oll <- ollama_backend("gemma4:31b")
b <- instrument(c(tone = "Is this sentence positive?"),
  labels = c("YES", "NO"))
res <- measure(parlasent, instrument = b, backend = oll, text = "sentence",
  id = "id", checkpoint = "ckpt")

# A run cut short leaves its finished documents in the directory.
res <- read_checkpoints("ckpt")
} # }
